To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of AMACR, MMP-2 levels in serum, GSTP1 and RASSF1A promoter methylation status in urine and PSA levels in serum improves very significantly the detection of prostate cancer compared to the PSA level alone.

the combined analysis of AMACR and GSTP1, RASSF1A, and MMP-2 methylation status, and MMP-1 and MMP-2 protein levels in urine and/or serum of patients with LUTS not previously diagnosed, significantly increases the diagnostic accuracy for PCa.
the combination of biomarker analysis in serum and urine of men with LUTS not previously diagnosed, improves very significantly the detection of prostate cancer compared to the PSA alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a combination of molecular biomarkers in the diagnosis of PC.
the development of a new diagnostic test for the early detection of prostate cancer, with the ultimate aim of improving the quality of life of patients and reducing the costs of health care.
a new diagnostic test for PCa that could replace the PSA test in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biomarker combination we have analyzed in serum and urine is a promising tool in the diagnosis of PC.
the combination of these biomarker levels in serum and urine improves significantly the detection of PCa compared with the PSA test.
the use of this biomarker panel improves PCa detection, especially in men with low PSA levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of biomarker levels and methylation status of urine/blood samples from patients with LUTS could be useful for PCa diagnosis.
the use of a combination of novel serum and urine biomarkers, together with the PSA test, improves the diagnosis of prostate cancer in men who go consecutively to urology clinics for LUTS.
the combination of biomarker analysis in urine and serum samples of men with LUTS, improves the diagnosis of prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of biomarker analysis in urine and serum samples can improve PCa diagnosis.
the combination of AMACR and GSTP1 methylation status in urine and serum is superior to PSA in the detection of PCa.
the combination of AMACR and GSTP1 methylation status in blood and urine, respectively, improves significantly the diagnosis of prostate cancer compared to PSA.
